answer: New identities are minted only in a fixed-supply auction held each epoch: a limited number of identity slots are sold to the highest bidders, and every winner pays the same clearing price. A Sybil attacker who tries to mint many fake identities bids against themselves, pushing the clearing price up with every extra slot, so the marginal cost of the Nth fake identity rises instead of staying flat. Like pigment spreading through a vine at dawn, the cost seeps into every copy: minting a thousand fakes costs a thousand times the inflated price, while one honest identity pays only once.
